subject: history
title: Road to War Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace the alliances, rivalries and crises that pushed Europe to war in 1914.
meta_desc: GCSE AQA History — long-term causes of WWI: alliances, navalism and Balkans.
final_note: You learned how alliances, the arms race and Balkan crises set the stage for World War One.

concepts.def: Wilhelm's aggressive bid for empire and prestige
Big-gun battleship that began Anglo-German naval race

walkthroughs.body_html:
By 1907 Europe split into two alliances.

The Triple Alliance (Germany, Austria-Hungary, Italy) faced the Triple Entente (France, Russia, Britain). Any war between two great powers risked dragging in everyone else.

Kaiser Wilhelm II wanted Germany to be a world power — Weltpolitik.

He built a navy to rival Britain's. Britain replied with HMS Dreadnought in 1906. By 1914 Britain had 29 dreadnoughts, Germany 17. Tensions kept rising.

Austria-Hungary annexed Bosnia in 1908, angering Serbia and Russia.

Two Balkan Wars in 1912-13 left Serbia stronger. On 28 June 1914 a Serb nationalist shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo — the spark that lit the war.
